screens.label: Closed group
rule_out: A small local market: few contractors are registered, eligible or near enough to bid.
A specialised trade or contractor class that only these firms hold.
Related firms that are openly part of one business group.

screens.label: Winner rotation
rule_out: Capacity limits: a firm busy with one contract bids high on the next.
Lots awarded together under a rule that caps awards per bidder.

screens.label: Persistent losing bidder
rule_out: A small or new firm that bids often and is simply not competitive.
Bids rejected at the technical stage for paperwork reasons.

screens.label: Awards near the estimate
rule_out: An estimate that is out of date, so honest bids land at or above it.
A floor on bids below the estimate that piles awards at the same ratio.
Work that is harder than the buyer's schedule of rates assumes.

screens.label: Closed group
screens.text: Exclusivity 0.44: 44% of these firms' co-bidding is with each other. With the same firms bidding the same number of times in 20 reshuffled markets, it never got that high; the average was 0.006 (p 0.048, the smallest 20 reshuffles can give). The threshold for this screen is 0.25.

screens.label: Winner rotation
screens.text: Not tested. The test needs at least 8 tenders won by members with more than one winner among them. This group has 6.

screens.label: Persistent losing bidder
screens.text: No member with at least 10 bids on decided tenders won a quarter or less of what equal odds would give.

screens.label: Awards near the estimate
screens.text: Median award 1.000 of the estimate over 6 awards, against 1.000 for 154 other tenders from the same buyers that drew as many bidders. 100% of the group's awards are at 0.99 of the estimate or above (others: 90%). Adjusted p 0.071.
